what_its_for: Glimepiride is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by helping your pancreas release more insulin, which lowers your blood sugar. It is used along with a healthy diet and regular exercise.
how_to_take: Take glimepiride by mouth once a day with your first main meal of the day (usually breakfast). Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Always take it at the same time each day. Do not skip meals after taking this medicine, as this can cause your blood sugar to drop too low.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose, usually 1 mg or 2 mg once daily, and may slowly increase it based on how your blood sugar responds. The maximum dose is usually 8 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if you are about to eat your main meal. If you have already skipped that meal or it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store glimepiride at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking glimepiride, as it can cause your blood sugar to drop too low or cause unpredictable reactions. Avoid skipping meals or eating less than usual without talking to your doctor first. Be careful with heavy exercise, as this can also lower your blood sugar. Avoid driving or operating machinery if you feel dizzy, shaky, or confused, as these may be signs of low blood sugar.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) such as shaking, sweating, dizziness, fast heartbeat, confusion, or fainting. Also call your doctor if you notice signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurry vision. Seek emergency help immediately if you have a severe allergic reaction with symptoms like rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Contact your doctor if you develop a skin rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual bruising or bleeding.
when_it_works: Glimepiride starts working within 2 to 3 hours after you take it. However, it may take several days to weeks to see the full effect on your blood sugar levels. Keep taking it every day as directed, even if you feel fine, because type 2 diabetes often has no noticeable symptoms.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with caution. Older adults are more sensitive to low blood sugar. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be right for you. Pregnancy: This medicine is not recommended during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor about safer options for managing blood sugar while pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if glimepiride passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Glimepiride is not approved for use in children.
